functional_semantics.triton: B = elementwise copy of A into a fresh empty_like buffer, same dtype, flat N*N addressing (impl_triton.py 14-18, 36).
functional_semantics.cutile: B = elementwise copy of A into a fresh empty_like buffer, same dtype, flat N*N addressing via A.contiguous().view(-1) / B.view(-1) (impl_cutile.py 17-19, 34, 38-39).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise the reference B = A + 0 (impl_torch.py 5) as a bit-exact copy; the reference's add-zero differs only for -0.0 (becomes +0.0), which value comparison cannot observe.

stages.triton: One kernel, one launch of ceil(N*N / tile) programs, load-then-store (impl_triton.py 8-18, 40-50).
stages.cutile: One kernel, one launch of ceil(N*N / tile) CTAs, load-then-store (impl_cutile.py 15-19, 59-64).

dependencies.triton: No inter-stage dependencies; each program is independent (impl_triton.py 14-18).
dependencies.cutile: No inter-stage dependencies; each CTA is independent (impl_cutile.py 17-19).

precision.triton: No arithmetic; values moved in the input dtype for fp16/bf16/fp32/int8 (impl_triton.py 17-18).
precision.cutile: No arithmetic; values moved in the input dtype (impl_cutile.py 18-19).

preprocessing.triton: Allocates B = empty_like(A) and computes total = N*N; passes A as-is (impl_triton.py 36-37).
preprocessing.cutile: Allocates B = empty_like(A); flattens via A.contiguous().view(-1) and B.view(-1), metadata-only for the contiguous generator input (impl_cutile.py 34, 38-39).
preprocessing.note: The flatten views move no bytes; no cast, pack or cached preprocessing on either side.

mutation.triton: A is read-only; fresh B every call (impl_triton.py 17, 36).
mutation.cutile: A is read-only; fresh B every call (impl_cutile.py 18, 34).
mutation.note: Neither side mutates the input; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: Both timed run() bodies read N*N elements once and write N*N elements once with no preprocessing traffic and nothing prepacked, which is exactly what bytes_expr counts; flops_expr is a nominal one-op-per-element figure for an operator with no arithmetic (config.yaml 14-15).
